# Instagram Song Finder by The Atom

> Instagram Song Finder is a free web tool, built and published by The Atom, that finds the ISRC (International Standard Recording Code) of a song and copies it in the form Instagram's music search accepts, for example `isrc:USUM72409273`. It needs no account. It is an independent tool and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Instagram, Meta or Spotify.

- Website: https://instagramsongfinder.theatom.lk/
- Publisher: The Atom (https://www.theatom.lk)
- Price: free, with no sign-up, login or usage limit for normal use
- Language: English
- Contact: info@theatom.lk

## What it does

A visitor identifies one specific recording of a song and gets its ISRC with the `isrc:` prefix already added. Pasting that string into the music search of an Instagram Story or Reel asks Instagram for that exact recording, instead of a cover, remix, live take or sped-up edit that a search by name often returns first.

## Ways to find a song

All of these go into the same search box, which works out what it was given.

- Song title, artist name, both together, part of a title, or keywords
- An ISRC, written plain (`USUM72409273`), hyphenated (`US-UM7-24-09273`) or prefixed (`isrc:USUM72409273`)
- A song link from a music service:
  - Spotify track links, share links and `spotify:track:` URIs: the exact recording when Spotify's catalog is reachable, otherwise a title search presented as possible matches
  - Deezer track links: the exact recording
  - Apple Music song links: matched by title, artist and length
  - YouTube and YouTube Music links: the video title is searched and the visitor picks the recording
  - SoundCloud track links: the track title is searched and the visitor picks the recording

Misspelled queries are tolerated. When nothing matches as typed, the closest results are shown and labelled as approximate.

Not supported: Tidal and Amazon Music links, and links to albums, playlists, artists or podcasts, because an ISRC belongs to a single recording.

## What a result shows

- Title, artists, album, release date and length
- Official album artwork
- Labels for distinct versions such as Live, Remastered, Remix, Acoustic and Sped up
- The ISRC, and the ready-to-paste string `isrc:<CODE>`
- A button that plays the catalog's official 30-second preview clip, where one exists
- One-tap copy, and a shortcut that copies the code and opens Instagram

Each recording is listed separately with its own ISRC. Different versions of a song are different recordings and are never merged.

## Where the data comes from

Song metadata and ISRC codes come from the official Spotify Web API where that integration is available, and otherwise from Deezer's public catalog. Apple's public lookup, and the public title information of YouTube and SoundCloud, are used only to identify which song a pasted link refers to. Codes are shown exactly as the catalog reports them. They are never generated, guessed or estimated. When a catalog has no ISRC for a recording, the site says "ISRC unavailable for this recording."

## Important limitations

- An ISRC identifies one sound recording. It does not show whether Instagram has licensed or indexed that recording.
- Searching Instagram by ISRC is not an officially documented Instagram feature. It may behave differently by account type, region and app version, and a correct code can still return no result.
- The site cannot check whether a song is available on Instagram. No public Instagram service reports that.
- A song can be on Spotify or Deezer and missing from Instagram, or the other way round, because each service licenses music separately.
- Not every recording is in the catalogs searched, so some songs will not be found.

## How to use the code on Instagram

1. Search for the song or paste its link.
2. Select the correct recording, using the details and the preview clip to confirm it.
3. Copy the `isrc:` string.
4. Open Instagram and start a Story or a Reel.
5. Open the music picker and paste the string into its search.
6. Select the song if Instagram returns the matching recording.

## Facts about ISRC

- ISRC stands for International Standard Recording Code and is defined by ISO 3901.
- It has 12 characters: a 2-letter prefix, a 3-character registrant code, a 2-digit year and a 5-digit designation.
- It identifies a recording, not a song. One song usually has several ISRCs, one per recorded version.
- The same recording normally keeps one ISRC across the services and releases it appears on.

## Privacy in brief

No accounts and no advertising or tracking cookies. Visits are counted with cookieless analytics.
